chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Ward Pinkett as friend and roommate
summary: Caldwell and Ward Pinkett were buddies; Pinkett was a nice trumpeter of part Indian descent who stayed with the group.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Yeah. So Thomas Morris, Willie really (unintelligible) in 1926. Gant's Ramblers, summer
This was when you were at Small's Paradise (unintelligible)?
That's right. (Unintelligible), Oh, Ward Pinkett quite a few. He picked guys up (unintelligible).
Ward Pinkett No, I didn't, you knew him?
Oh, we were buddies. We were buddies, roomed together.
Well, what's the story on him? What sort of a guy was he?

He was a nice trumpet player, and through the years -- on his mother's side was part Indian, like my -- my great-grandfather was an old Indian chief. And Ward could pass, but he wouldn't. And like the bands, like with the (unintelligible) rumba bands at the time was bigger, late the time, in the early '50's and '60's, and early Ward, like he born in Virginia. His father had a big tailor shop there, and he wouldn't go. He just stayed right there with the group, working around. He worked with Jelly too, (unin- Mode telligible) a lot of records with Jelly.
